_readme: Review summaries show 'Coming soon' in the app for any hospital without an entry here. Keys must be the hospital's exact OpenStreetMap 'name' tag, lowercased (see insurance-data.json's _readme for naming gotchas). Entries added here are based on actually reading real reviews (Google Maps, etc.) as of the noted date — not invented. Format: "some hospital name": { "rating": 4.2, "reviewCount": 500, "asOf": "2026-09", "summary": "..." }. Two optional fields, both sourced directly from Google's own review data (never estimated/invented): "ratingBreakdown" is the exact [5-star, 4-star, 3-star, 2-star, 1-star] review counts; "topics" is a list of [label, mentionCount] pairs from Google's own extracted review topics, lightly curated to drop mistranslated or nonsensical chips. Leave both out entirely if you didn't capture the real numbers — don't approximate them from the prose summary.

the mount sinai hospital.summary: Mixed reviews overall. Recurring praise: several patients single out specific doctors and nurses — especially in the ER and oncology/cancer care — for compassionate, attentive treatment during difficult visits. Recurring complaints: long wait times, inconsistent communication, and follow-up/aftercare that some families felt was disorganized for complex, ongoing conditions. Based on reading a sample of reviews plus Google's review-topic tags (nurses, phone calls, cancer, and follow-up messaging were the most-mentioned topics).

massachusetts general hospital.summary: Ratings are bimodal (mostly 5-star and 1-star), which is typical for large hospitals. Strong recurring praise for the Labor & Delivery unit and ER, with patients repeatedly naming individual nurses as compassionate and reassuring, plus several accounts of life-saving specialist treatment for rare or complex conditions. The most serious complaints come from high-risk patients who felt dismissed or discharged too early, alongside general front-desk/communication friction.

johns hopkins hospital.summary: Sharply bimodal ratings (565 five-star vs. 411 one-star out of 1,116). Positive reviews consistently praise nursing and medical staff's compassion and expertise for complex care such as cancer treatment and childbirth. The Emergency Department is by far the most-discussed and most-complained-about topic (107 mentions of "ER" alone in Google's topic tags), with recurring accounts of long waits and a confusing, impersonal intake process.

cedars-sinai medical center.summary: Nurses get the most topic mentions of any hospital reviewed here (74), with real praise for clinical care and specialists who coordinated urgent transfers/interventions patients credit with major outcomes. But there's a serious recurring complaint pattern: multiple reviewers cite ER wait times of 8+ hours, non-medical/support staff described as curt or unhelpful especially toward families in ICU waiting areas, and some complaints about facility cleanliness and upkeep.

nyu langone health - tisch hospital.summary: Notably more consistently positive than the other major hospitals summarized here. Recurring themes: warm, attentive nursing staff; strong maternity/labor-and-delivery experiences called out by multiple reviewers; and positive accounts of complex surgical and cardiac care with patients naming specific doctors as thorough and reassuring. Fewer visible complaints in this sample, though the ER is still a frequently-mentioned topic.

vancouver general hospital.summary: Nurses are the single most-mentioned topic of any hospital in this set (87 mentions), with many reviewers naming specific surgeons, nurses, and anesthesiologists as skilled and compassionate — including for major procedures like cancer surgery and for patients with years of repeat ER visits for chronic conditions. Some reviews reflect broader frustration with Canada's public healthcare system and wait times generally rather than hospital-specific complaints; a few cite occasional communication friction with ER staff.

삼성서울병원.summary: Highest average rating among the hospitals summarized here. Nursing staff are strongly and repeatedly praised, especially on specialized wards like oncology, described as highly professional and compassionate. The most common complaint is practical rather than clinical: the multi-building campus (main building, annex, cancer center) is confusing to navigate, with reviewers citing unclear maps/signage and inconsistent directions from staff. A few reviewers found checkup-style visits felt rushed or impersonal. English name: Samsung Medical Center.

cleveland clinic.summary: Reviews reflect the hospital's specialty reputation — multiple reviewers praise complex cardiac surgery, organ transplant, and complicated GI/surgical cases, several explicitly comparing it favorably to other top-tier hospitals (Mayo Clinic, Northwestern). Front-desk/admissions staff are specifically praised for helping arrange urgent transfers from other hospitals. Recurring complaints center on billing/invoicing disputes (frequent enough that an ombudsman process is commonly mentioned) and occasional inconsistent care on specific wards during single admissions, even among patients with otherwise good histories there.

stanford hospital.summary: Smaller review sample than most hospitals here. Most reviews are strongly positive, with patients naming specific doctors and describing attentive, respectful nursing care and successful treatment for serious conditions — one reviewer credits the team with extending a parent's life with myelofibrosis. The most serious complaint in this sample: a patient with a broken ankle says they were turned away without treatment, unfavorably contrasting it with a nearby hospital that operated within 24 hours.

newyork-presbyterian / weill cornell med.summary: Bimodal ratings (558 five-star vs. 260 one-star). Positive reviews praise knowledgeable, dedicated nurses and doctors, world-class specialists, and continuously upgraded facilities/amenities. Google's topic tags point to the Emergency Department, bed availability, and security as the most-discussed subjects — including at least one serious complaint about a conflict with ER staff that escalated to hospital security.

duke university hospital.summary: Sharply bimodal ratings (459 five-star vs. 355 one-star, unusually close for this set). Every review readable in this sample was strongly positive, specifically praising the nursing staff (the single most-mentioned topic, 66 mentions) as excellent and well-coordinated. Given the large one-star share and topic tags around waiting rooms, front desk, and walking distances on the sprawling campus, the negative half likely centers on wait times and campus logistics rather than clinical quality — though no negative review surfaced directly in this sample to confirm that.

houston methodist hospital.summary: Nursing staff are the dominant positive theme (84 topic mentions, among the highest of any hospital in this set), and multiple reviewers specifically praise the transplant program for treating patients compassionately regardless of age or insurance status. Every review readable in this sample was strongly positive — private rooms, attentive staff, specific nurses and aides named gratefully. No serious complaints surfaced, though this is a small slice of 1,189 total reviews.

northwestern memorial hospital.summary: Bimodal ratings (601 five-star vs. 365 one-star). Detailed review text was limited in the available sample (Google showed a restricted view), but the most substantive account describes a very positive birth/delivery experience with attentive staff. Topic tags point to the Emergency Department as by far the most-discussed subject (61 mentions, more than any other topic), alongside waiting rooms and security — consistent with ER wait times likely driving much of the negative share, though no detailed negative review could be read directly to confirm that.

denver health medical center.summary: One of the higher average ratings and largest review counts in this set (2,217 five-star vs. 680 one-star). Nurses are by far the most-discussed topic (139 mentions). Specialty clinics get specific praise — bariatric surgery and ophthalmology patients describe efficient, attentive, professional care with named providers. The clearest complaint theme: at least one detailed account of a nurse behaving unprofessionally and dismissively toward a patient's family in front of student nurses, raising concerns about training culture, though this was one specific account rather than a dominant pattern in the sample read.

hospital of the university of pennsylvan.summary: Bimodal ratings (337 five-star vs. 279 one-star). Positive reviews describe attentive nursing care and a comfortable overall stay. But there are specific, detailed negative accounts: one high-risk pregnancy patient felt maternal-fetal medicine specialists seemed uncertain about her case despite transferring there specifically for their expertise, and another visitor describes inconsistent, confusing visiting-hours enforcement. Topic tags around room assignment, triage, and waiting suggest logistics and communication are recurring friction points.

vanderbilt university medical center.summary: Bimodal ratings (717 five-star vs. 450 one-star). Nurses are the most-mentioned topic (100), with reviewers specifically praising diagnostic accuracy and successful surgical intervention after other hospitals had missed a diagnosis. Inpatient stays get consistent praise for cleanliness and courteous staff. The ER is the clearest recurring weak point: multiple complaints describe cramped, dirty waiting areas, hallway beds, and at least one account of being pressed for payment during an emergency visit.

emory university hospital.summary: Bimodal ratings (771 five-star vs. 301 one-star). Cancer care draws specific, detailed praise — one reviewer calls it the best place for cancer treatment, crediting a named oncologist and the radiation/chemo teams for thorough communication and side-effect management. A liver transplant patient's account is more mixed: steady pre-transplant care, but communication with the radiology department's leadership was described as "the worst," and the patient felt under-informed about the transplant process itself despite years of prior treatment.

jackson memorial hospital.summary: The lowest average rating among the hospitals summarized here, despite most individual reviews readable in this sample being quite positive about clinical care: nurses are consistently praised by name and role — a burn patient with 65%+ body burns and a grandmother's fall/hospitalization both single out nursing care as excellent. Topic tags (phone communication, finance/billing, and even lawsuits and hospital leadership) suggest the lower overall average is driven more by operational and administrative friction than bedside care. One detailed pregnancy-related review described a complication-filled C-section day but was cut off before its resolution.

banner university medical center phoenix.summary: Nurses dominate the topic tags by a wide margin (218 mentions, the highest of any hospital in this set), and specialty teams get extensive individual praise — rheumatology, cardiology, and liver-disease specialists are named for accurate diagnosis and thorough communication. Topic tags point to a strong maternity/NICU and stroke/cardiac program (baby, C-section, NICU, stroke, cardiac surgery, and heart transplant are all frequently mentioned). Reviews sampled were predominantly very positive, describing compassionate care during frightening health crises; no serious complaint surfaced directly in this sample.

mayo clinic saint marys campus.summary: Every review readable in this sample was strongly positive, consistently naming specific surgeons, nurses, and care teams — a pattern of gratitude reviews thanking individual staff across pre-op, surgery, and recovery. Reviewers specifically praise the combination of advanced, specialized medicine (heart surgery, throat surgery) with attentive, compassionate bedside care, and note comfortable accommodations including private rooms and visitor sofa beds. No negative themes surfaced in this sample.

virginia mason hospital & seattle medica.summary: Clinical care draws strong individual praise — patients name specific doctors (a gastroenterologist, a knee-replacement team) for making them feel genuinely cared for and respected, not just processed. The most detailed complaint here is different from typical hospital gripes: a 50-year patient describes the hospital's merger with Franciscan Health/CHI as damaging the patient experience, citing an understaffed front desk and 30-minute check-in waits as a direct consequence of post-merger management decisions rather than clinical care itself. Billing/invoicing is also a notably frequent topic tag.

st. paul's hospital.summary: Every review readable in this sample was strongly positive, with patients consistently naming specific doctors, nurses, and midwives across surgery, maternity, ER, and gynecology for skilled, compassionate, multilingual care — interpretation services were specifically praised twice. Topic tags around homelessness and addiction reflect the hospital's downtown Vancouver location serving a population with significant social needs, alongside general commentary about Canada's healthcare system seen at other Canadian hospitals in this set. No negative review surfaced in this sample.

uc medical center moffett & long hospita.summary: Strong recurring praise for neurology, organ transplant, and women's health specialties, with multiple reviewers describing cutting-edge treatment and clear, compassionate communication from staff — one credits a neurological procedure with saving her husband's life. The most serious concern in this sample is a single review containing an unverified, uncorroborated allegation of a patient death from an anesthesia error during brain surgery; this is one reviewer's claim that cannot be confirmed, not an established fact, but it exists in the review record. Parking is also flagged as difficult, with a shuttle recommended. English name: UCSF Medical Center.

nyc health + hospitals/bellevue.summary: The highest average rating and by far the largest review count among the hospitals summarized here. Despite the strong overall average, the specific reviews readable in this sample were more mixed than that number suggests: alongside genuine praise (helpful front-desk staff who remember patients by name, complimentary transportation services, a surgeon praised for good doctor-patient rapport), there are also serious complaints about neglectful or unresponsive nursing care and one account of a 10+ hour ER wait described as "torture." "Caution"/warning-style mentions were the single most frequent topic tag (175 mentions, more than any other hospital in this set) — worth reading a wider sample given how large and heterogeneous this hospital's patient population and services are.

서울대학교병원.summary: A much smaller review sample than most hospitals in this set. Reviewers consistently praise SNUH's medical and diagnostic quality and its reputation as one of Korea's top hospitals for handling serious or complex illness — several call it the best in the country. But more than one reviewer specifically notes that the bedside-manner/service experience doesn't match the clinical quality, describing accurate, non-over-treating care at reasonable prices but limited warmth. Parking is also flagged as a practical annoyance due to ongoing construction. English name: Seoul National University Hospital.

서울아산병원.summary: Skews positive overall (314 five-star vs. 88 one-star). Topic tags point to nurses as the most-discussed subject, alongside hospital systems/policies, parking, and waiting times. One reviewer describes the integrated nursing-care ward's strict no-visitor, no-direct-family-drop-off policy as inconvenient, though this reflects hospital policy rather than a service failure; the underground parking garage in the newer building is also described as confusing, with many opting for external parking instead. Reviews read were otherwise positive but light on detail. English name: Asan Medical Center.

세브란스병원.summary: Bimodal-leaning ratings (306 five-star vs. 110 one-star). A pediatric ward nurse is specifically named and praised for comforting anxious parents around children's surgery with warmth and kindness — nursing care is the most-mentioned topic (21). One detailed negative account specifically warns against the dental department, describing residents and interns treating a patient without gloves or masks before the attending physician's exam, and feeling uncomfortably stared at post-surgery. Waiting times and cost are also frequently-mentioned topics. English name: Severance Hospital.

가톨릭대학교 서울성모병원.summary: One of the higher average ratings among the Korean hospitals summarized here. Reviewers consistently place it among Korea's "Big 5" hospitals, praising overwhelming facility quality and cleanliness, with staff generally described as kind. Recurring notes are practical rather than clinical: the campus is very large and can be hard to navigate to find a specific ward, it isn't directly subway-connected (a street crossing is needed), and driving there is discouraged in favor of transit. English name: Seoul St. Mary's Hospital (The Catholic University of Korea).

강북삼성병원.summary: Praise centers on specialized departments — a dedicated hand-surgery orthopedics unit is called out for more expert care — and one striking account from a long-time US resident visiting Korea who needed emergency treatment for a sudden respiratory crisis, calling the staff's systematic coordination outstanding. Recurring practical complaints: surgery scheduling can take a long time (similar to other general hospitals), and parking is a significant pain point during ongoing facility expansion, with waits up to 30 minutes just to enter the garage. English name: Kangbuk Samsung Hospital.

이대목동병원.summary: The lowest average rating and most negative-leaning reviews among the Korean hospitals summarized here. One reviewer had a good first-visit experience with helpful reception and clear directions staff, but others describe serious problems: a rude call-center interaction over rescheduling a follow-up appointment, an ER intake nurse allegedly turning away a patient who'd already received some treatment elsewhere, and one detailed account of a failed surgery that led to a lawsuit and a court-mediated settlement without the reviewer ever receiving an apology. Nurses and wait times are the most-discussed topics. English name: Ewha Womans University Mokdong Hospital.

건국대학교병원.summary: Ward 82 and its neurosurgery-department nursing staff are repeatedly and specifically praised as warm and caring across multiple reviews. But there's a recurring administrative complaint: one reviewer describes hospital management and policies — illustrated by wheelchair-availability issues — as burdensome despite "patient-centered" signage, and another criticizes a specific attending neurosurgeon's dismissive, smirking bedside manner when discussing a patient's condition with family, alongside describing ICU shift handoffs as disorganized. Accessibility (direct subway connection) and facility quality get consistent praise. English name: Konkuk University Medical Center.

한양대학교의료원.summary: Every review readable in this sample was positive about clinical care — attending physicians explain things clearly, nurses are attentive on repeat visits, and one reviewer credits systematic inpatient rounds and monitoring for reassurance during a parent's hospitalization. The single most consistent complaint isn't about care quality at all: the hospital sits on a steep hill, making it hard to walk to from the subway, with multiple reviewers recommending the shuttle bus or the internal connecting corridors and elevators between buildings instead. English name: Hanyang University Seoul Hospital.

아주대학교병원.summary: A more negative-leaning sample than most hospitals in this set (note: Google splits this campus across several listings — this uses the one sharing the hospital's exact address with the largest review count). A specific nephrology professor is praised for thorough, accurate care, and older reviews call it one of the country's best by reputation and scale. But recent reviews include serious concerns: a detailed account of a doctor's insensitive reaction during a cancer diagnosis, a strong warning against the pediatrics department for alleged over-treatment, misdiagnosis, and repeated billing charges, and one review referencing the loss of a child that hopes for a full investigation — a serious, unverified claim that cannot be confirmed but exists in the review record. Parking is also flagged as difficult. English name: Ajou University Hospital, nationally known for its Level I trauma center, though these specific reviews didn't discuss that program.

부산대학교병원.summary: Bimodal-leaning ratings (141 five-star vs. 54 one-star). One reviewer credits a neurosurgery professor with successful emergency treatment of a ruptured brain aneurysm (subarachnoid hemorrhage) during a holiday, expressing strong gratitude. Good public-transit accessibility is repeatedly noted (very close to a subway station). Recurring complaints: long waits even with an appointment (about 2 hours for routine ophthalmology testing was cited), and specifically poor front-desk communication at one building — large monitors blocking the reception counter and staff speaking too quietly to be heard, which one reviewer says is especially hard on elderly patients. English name: Pusan National University Hospital, Busan.

evanston hospital.summary: One of the most polarized ratings in this set (193 five-star vs. 197 one-star, nearly an even split). Positive reviews describe responsive staff and good psychiatric and maternity care experiences. But there's a striking negative account: a patient describes a specialist who left mid-appointment to make a personal dinner reservation call, dismissed their symptoms, and then billed over $200 for the visit. The Emergency Department is by far the most-discussed topic overall (64 mentions). Now branded Endeavor Health Evanston Hospital (formerly NorthShore).

edward hospital.summary: One of the highest average ratings and largest review counts in this set. Nurses are overwhelmingly the most-praised element (192 mentions), with reviewers crediting them for compassionate care through everything from a pediatric needle-phobia visit to a 37-day ICU stay to childbirth. The most detailed complaint is narrower: a post-gastrectomy patient says staff failed to track her restricted diet throughout her stay, resulting in an inappropriate meal being sent on discharge day. Part of Endeavor Health (formerly Edward-Elmhurst Health).

osf saint francis medical center.summary: Very bimodal (273 five-star vs. 256 one-star, nearly even). ER wait times are a serious, recurring complaint: multiple reviewers describe 4-7 hour waits with minimal care (basic tests but no physician visit) and dismissed pain concerns. One reviewer alleges serious documentation and protocol inconsistencies around a labor-and-delivery case — a serious claim that cannot be verified but is present in the review record. On the positive side, reviewers single out specific named surgeons for good post-surgical recovery support, with one noting the hospital's quality has recently improved after a period of poor reputation.

saint anthony medical center.summary: ER experiences are highly mixed: some reviewers praise clear communication and attentive nurses even through long waits, while others describe overnight staff needing improvement and unattended waits. The most serious complaint is a maternity account: a first-time mother says she was left unattended for 8 hours awaiting labor induction, that her doctor made delivery decisions unilaterally without consulting her, and that postpartum care for both her and the baby was inadequate. Branded OSF Saint Anthony Medical Center.

uw health swedishamerican hospital.summary: Radiology and imaging staff draw specific praise for going out of their way to make anxious patients comfortable — one reviewer describes staff playing requested music and offering a blindfold during an MRI to ease claustrophobia, another describes a staff member personally driving them home. One notable mistake: an ultrasound technician revealed a baby's sex despite the patient repeatedly asking not to know, ahead of a planned gender-reveal party. The most serious complaint describes being stuck in a shared room with a disruptive roommate for four days, with repeated room-change requests ignored by both nurses and a supervisor.

memorial medical center.summary: The lowest average rating among the Illinois hospitals summarized here. ICU care draws specific, strong praise — a named nurse is singled out for exceptional care during a family member's repeated stroke-related hospitalizations — but front-desk and general ward experiences are a recurring problem: multiple reviewers describe rude or dismissive staff, ignored call bells, and confusing ER triage order with 6+ hour waits and no explanation given. Understaffing is explicitly named as a topic by one reviewer; another criticizes visitor-badge security procedures as excessive during an already stressful ICU stay. Now branded Springfield Memorial Hospital.

carle foundation hospital.summary: Nursing care draws strong specific praise across serious cases — childbirth (two nurses thanked by name), a father's fall with multiple fractures, and ICU-level infection care for a patient transferred from out of state. But insurance/billing is the second-most-mentioned topic overall (49 mentions, just behind nurses), suggesting billing disputes are a significant recurring friction point, and one reviewer describes a nurse rushing physical therapy and pushing early medication administration against the patient's own schedule. ER wait times are also frequently flagged, though several reviewers say the subsequent inpatient care made up for it.

경북대학교병원.summary: A smaller review sample than most hospitals in this set. A specific cardiology doctor is praised by name for empathetic care, and the hospital carries strong regional prestige as Daegu's oldest and most representative hospital (100+ year history). But there are pointed complaints too: one reviewer describes a cancer specialist as unfriendly and uncooperative with other staff, and another describes a same-day procedure cancellation with only 1-2 hours' notice after the patient had rearranged their schedule. English name: Kyungpook National University Hospital, Daegu.

충남대학교병원.summary: A smaller review sample. The most consistent complaint is administrative: one reviewer describes the phone system as broken for months, with no way to reach the hospital or specific departments by phone, forcing in-person visits to get anything done. Positive reviews mention a broad range of specialty departments and note that ER staff worked hard for patients even during a busy shift. A couple of reviewers name specific doctors (an ophthalmology professor, a cardiology specialist) approvingly. English name: Chungnam National University Hospital, Daejeon.

전남대학교병원.summary: The smallest review sample among the Korean hospitals summarized here. Reviews are largely practical rather than clinical: reviewers describe the hospital as a huge, maze-like complex facing a rival hospital across the street, often overcrowded, with complaints about overflowing restroom trash and confusing corridor navigation. One reviewer describes urgent eye-care triage (a corneal ulcer) requiring an ER route since no ophthalmology appointment existed, and another still resents unclear, jargon-heavy consent-form paperwork from a past visit years ago. A brief positive review credits kind staff and a successful surgery. English name: Chonnam National University Hospital, Gwangju.

가천대 길병원.summary: A smaller review sample. Founded by a pioneering OB-GYN and now regarded as one of Incheon's largest general hospitals. The most frequently tagged complaint topic, despite the small sample, is "over-treatment" (과잉진료) — one reviewer describes extensive testing, including an MRI, for wrist pain that ultimately resulted in medication only, feeling the workup was more extensive than the outcome warranted. Another reviewer calls it clean and solidly good for the Incheon area overall. English name: Gachon University Gil Medical Center, Incheon.

東京大学医学部附属病院.summary: Bimodal ratings (245 five-star vs. 162 one-star). Topic tags are dominated by administrative themes rather than clinical ones: health checkups (77 mentions, the most of any topic), billing (37), and referral letters (25) — consistent with this being one of Japan's flagship "special function" teaching hospitals, which charge an extra fee to patients who arrive without a referral letter from a smaller clinic. Reviews mention nickel-and-dime fees (e.g. paid Wi-Fi in general wards) and note that as a teaching hospital, trainees may be present during procedures. English name: The University of Tokyo Hospital.

聖路加国際病院.summary: This hospital's international-patient orientation shows clearly in its reviews: several are from travelers who needed emergency care in Tokyo and specifically praise being treated with good English communication, patience, and kindness even during holiday or night hours when running on reduced staff. One detailed negative account accuses the hospital of stringing along a patient who requested an urgent MRI without actually expediting it — i.e. of prioritizing billable process over efficient care. Topic tags around referral letters and primary-physician requirements reflect the same "special function hospital" referral system seen at other major Japanese teaching hospitals. English name: St. Luke's International Hospital, Tokyo.

京都大学医学部附属病院.summary: Strong specific praise across multiple reviews: a long-time patient values the university hospital's thorough 40-50 minute appointments over quick small-clinic visits, a named orthopedic surgeon is praised as gentle and kind, and a Spanish traveler credits the entire emergency gallbladder surgery team — especially a named surgeon — with excellent, compassionate care despite a language barrier. The most pointed complaint singles out a specific gynecologist as dismissive and unwilling to listen, contrasted directly against another named doctor in the same review whom the patient calls excellent and trustworthy. English name: Kyoto University Hospital.

九州大学病院.summary: Bimodal ratings (203 five-star vs. 161 one-star). Clinical care draws real praise: a neurosurgery inpatient credits their attending doctor with clear, reassuring communication throughout hospitalization, and an OB-GYN patient describes midwives and nurses as gentle and calming during a high-risk first pregnancy. But there are pointed staff-conduct complaints unrelated to clinical care: a blood-draw nurse described as rushed and dismissive without eye contact, and a separate account of a non-clinical staff member behaving unprofessionally (sleeping on the job, reacting angrily to a minor request) in the hospital's public dining area. English name: Kyushu University Hospital, Fukuoka.

北海道大学病院.summary: Pediatric care draws consistent praise — multiple reviewers describe doctors speaking gently and patiently even with anxious or resistant child patients. Complaints are mostly about communication and process clarity rather than harshness: one patient missed being called for an X-ray because a separate, unannounced registration step wasn't explained; another describes some doctors giving overly technical answers or multitasking while talking rather than being fully present. On-site amenities (a café, a convenience store, even a small plant greenhouse) get an unusually detailed practical shoutout from one reviewer. English name: Hokkaido University Hospital, Sapporo.

名古屋大学医学部附属病院.summary: Inpatient clinical experiences draw strong praise — a cataract surgery patient credits kind nurses and better-than-expected hospital food, and a bladder cancer patient wrote a glowingly grateful review from their hospital bed the night before a successful discharge. But phone-based administrative contact is a serious sore point: one reviewer describes being placed on hold repeatedly by a switchboard operator who ultimately said a supervisor authorized hanging up on them mid-complaint. Health checkups and phone communication are the two most-discussed topics overall. English name: Nagoya University Hospital.

st thomas' hospital.summary: One of the higher average ratings and largest review counts in this set. Famously linked to Florence Nightingale's nursing legacy, and includes a COVID memorial wall on site that one visitor found moving. Topic tags point to the ER and maternity/midwifery services as the most-discussed aspects by far. The one detailed complaint readable in this sample is from a tourist who developed sudden tonsillitis: a very long wait just to complete registration paperwork, followed by another long wait for treatment — a pattern consistent with general NHS emergency department demand rather than anything specific to this hospital.

campus charité mitte.summary: The main campus listing (3.0/267) carries little review detail itself. Its Emergency Department has a separate, far more heavily-reviewed listing (2.4/533) that likely better reflects most patients' actual experience: positive accounts describe fast, professional, reassuring care for serious allergic reactions and sudden chest pain, but the most detailed complaint notes that despite Charité's global reputation (one reviewer cites a top-10 world ranking), the ER itself feels outdated and undersized for the hospital's scale — that reviewer waited 6 hours despite the department not appearing particularly busy. Charité is split across several campuses in OSM/Google; this covers Campus Charité Mitte specifically.

hôpital pitié-salpêtrière.summary: One of the largest review counts in this set, and sharply split. Some reviewers praise the hospital's overall medical reputation and competence as "undisputed" and efficient across nearly every specialty, describing staff as attentive and warm. But there are serious complaints too, especially around the maternity ward — one reviewer describes being assigned a room with substandard hygiene and amenities for four days around a scheduled delivery. ER wait times also draw sharp sarcasm from at least one reviewer describing multi-hour waits. Notably, dental emergencies and oral medicine are the single most-discussed topics in Google's tag summary, suggesting the hospital's dental/oral emergency department draws particular reviewer attention.

royal prince alfred hospital.summary: Multiple Korean-speaking patients specifically highlight the hospital's Korean-language translation service as making a real difference in feeling cared for and understood during surgery and recovery. A cardiothoracic surgery patient names an entire care team — a professor surgeon, a specialist nurse, and ICU staff — with detailed gratitude, explicitly noting that the hospital's old, unglamorous Victorian-era buildings don't reflect the quality of its medical staff. No serious complaints surfaced in this sample.

singapore general hospital.summary: Ward and inpatient nursing care draw strong praise — a named ENT specialist and a specific ward's nursing staff are credited with a successful, reassuring salivary gland surgery recovery that one reviewer says "saved their life." But the Emergency Department is a clear sore point: one reviewer describes a staff member shouting a "last warning" at an elderly patient simply asking to use the bathroom, and another describes an ophthalmology emergency (sudden severe eye pain and vision loss) still unresolved after nearly 10 hours in the department, including a 3-hour wait just for an initial consultation.

taipei veterans general hospital.summary: One of the highest average ratings and by far the largest review count in this set. Nurses are the single most-mentioned topic by a wide margin (584 mentions), and reviews consistently praise them as experienced and attentive. The hospital is independently ranked Taiwan's #1 hospital and #174 globally by Newsweek/Statista's "World's Best Hospitals" list, with particular strength in cancer care (Taiwan's first heavy-ion cancer therapy center), cardiovascular disease, and geriatrics. Recurring complaints are minor and logistical rather than clinical: long waits even with appointments, scarce weekday parking, humid bathrooms, and slow elevators.

林口長庚紀念醫院.summary: One of the largest review counts in this set, and reputed as Taiwan's best private hospital by at least one reviewer. Multiple reviewers name specific department directors and nurses by name with detailed gratitude — an OB-GYN director and outpatient nurse for a laparoscopic surgery recovery, and a cardiac surgery director praised for weeks of consistent family communication during an ICU stay that involved weighing aggressive treatment against palliative care. The most pointed complaint is about a specific front-desk registration staff member described as rude to patients who are already unwell. English name: Chang Gung Memorial Hospital, Linkou.

china medical university hospital.summary: Unusually bimodal, with slightly more 1-star than 5-star reviews (812 vs. 753). Specific named specialists draw strong praise: an ophthalmologist credited with calm, skilled emergency treatment for a sudden retinal tear, and a nationally recognized neurosurgeon — previously head of neurosurgery at Taipei Veterans General, reportedly also treats a well-known Taiwanese celebrity — recommended for pituitary tumor surgery. But there's a sharply contrasting complaint about a specific dermatologist described as arrogant and dismissive, spending under 3 minutes on a visit without a proper examination. Nurses are by far the most-discussed topic overall (267 mentions). Located in Taichung.

aiims emergency.summary: As India's top-ranked public medical institution, treatment is free (fully government-funded), and one reviewer credits it with the country's best facilities and most experienced doctors — but notes that reaching that quality requires enduring long waits and heavy paperwork, with few patients feeling they truly benefit despite the public investment. Several detailed and serious complaints follow a similar pattern: patients describe being left uncommunicated-with on stretchers during apparent emergencies, one names a specific doctor as dangerously unprofessional, and another describes a father being admitted for planned surgery only to be discharged without treatment and redirected to a different hospital after all pre-op tests were completed. Note: only this hospital's Emergency Room is tagged as a distinct location in OpenStreetMap/Google — the main AIIMS New Delhi campus is much larger.

amsterdam umc locatie amc.summary: One patient calls it the best hospital they've ever been to, crediting quick, responsive care for post-surgical complications that arose two days after a difficult operation. But there's a sharply negative account too: a parent describes repeated pharmacy/prescription routing errors that left a child in pain for a full day, plus unhelpful, rushed phone support. A smaller, more unusual complaint: unsettling foot-related medical photos displayed in the hospital cafeteria.

hospital general de méxico.summary: As Mexico's flagship public general hospital, it draws real gratitude — one reviewer credits it with saving their mother's life via top specialists and fast emergency testing, specifically naming staff members (including one who keeps pet squirrels that made the wait more bearable), and calls it the best option for those who can't afford private care. But underfunding is a recurring, visible theme: reviewers describe a building badly needing remodeling, a chaotic ER stretcher/security process, a 2-day wait just to be moved to a ward, persistent bad odors, and many broken facilities — one reviewer explicitly concludes the public hospital is severely underfunded.

ciudad sanitaria la paz.summary: The Emergency Department is the dominant topic by far (307 mentions). One reviewer's account is particularly striking: they describe the physical facility as visibly aged and rundown "like a hospital in a developing country," citing poor staff welfare, inadequate hygiene, and a severely inadequate maintenance budget despite being one of Madrid's major hospitals. A separate reviewer describes feeling dismissed in the ER despite worsening neck pain and arm weakness after 10 days of ineffective prior treatment. Balancing this, another reviewer praises the medical staff broadly for combining strong professionalism with genuine empathy and attentive care for patients and families. Better known as La Paz University Hospital, Madrid.

hospital das clínicas.summary: Long-time patients describe deep personal loyalty — one reviewer has been treated here since childhood and calls it the best hospital they know, another was born here to parents who met while both working at the hospital and is still treated here today. Set against that, one reviewer describes a serious breakdown in care: arriving with a neurologist's admission referral, being shuffled between buildings, blocked from entering by security, and never actually attended to. Other complaints cite severe understaffing with three sequential check-in desks and hour-plus waits, unfriendly security guards, and dirty bathrooms. A separate listing for the hospital's emergency room ("Clinical Hospital FMUSP Emergency Room") is rated 4.1 from 213 reviews. Full name: Hospital das Clínicas da Faculdade de Medicina da Universidade de São Paulo.

北京协和医院.summary: Reviews are for the hospital's East Campus listing ("北京协和医院东院"), which has more reviews than the main-campus listing. One reviewer praises the international medical environment; a family credits neurosurgery department head Dr. Wang Renzhi, nurse Bao Xinjie, and gastroenterologist Dr. Xiao Yi by name for years of skilled, ethical care. A foreign patient's review is actually an inquiry about breast cancer treatment for a relative rather than feedback on care received here. Review volume is modest for a hospital of this size — treat the sample as limited. Full name: Peking Union Medical College Hospital (PUMCH), China's top-ranked hospital.

policlinico umberto i.summary: Ratings are sharply polarized (120 five-star vs. 103 one-star out of 286). On the positive side, one reviewer credits the Valdoni surgical ward with saving their life, praising the entire team as professional, kind, and skilled. On the negative side, one reviewer describes a relative's impetigo going undiagnosed and untreated, being isolated unnecessarily in a prefab ward with almost no visits and at least one missed dinner, and a family bathroom with no toilet paper — the family eventually left and got the condition diagnosed and treated within days by a small-town doctor. Another long-time patient says that over 18 years the facilities have aged and staff empathy has declined, describing the hospital as now feeling profit-driven. Frequently mentioned terms include nurses, professors, doctors, and "the healthcare system" generally. Opened in 1903 and affiliated with Sapienza University of Rome.

chris hani baragwanath hospital.summary: One reviewer calls it formerly the largest and best hospital in the world, now "on the verge of collapse," citing chronic drug shortages — a prostate cancer patient was given only 10 days' supply of medication with none in stock for a refill. Against that, a maternity patient describes excellent care throughout: security staff, doctors, and specifically the nurses of Ward 58 praised for patience, helping with breastfeeding and holding her newborn as a first-time mother. A reviewer alleges losing a brother-in-law to what they describe as an easily preventable death in June 2026, criticizing widespread carelessness, lack of empathy, and poor communication among staff — this is a serious, unverified allegation, not a confirmed incident. A family expresses gratitude by name to a Dr. De Freitas for attentive care of a sibling with ascites. Another describes a staff member's rude, dismissive behavior in the MVA department. One of the largest hospitals in the world by bed count, located in Soweto, Johannesburg.

hospital de pediatría \"profesor doctor.summary: Overwhelmingly positive, with thousands of parents publicly thanking specific departments and staff by name — one mother credits the gastroenterology team for her infant son's successful hernia surgery, another says the diagnosis and compassion she received here exceeded what she could get even with private insurance, and a patient treated here since age 7 (now 17) rates the facilities, cleanliness, and staff a perfect 10/10. The hospital's official account personally replies to many reviews with a recurring line: "Garrahan belongs to everyone." A minority of reviews are critical (1-star reviews are about 5% of the total), but the overwhelming pattern in visible reviews is gratitude. Widely regarded as one of Latin America's top pediatric hospitals.

uniwersyteckie centrum kliniczne wum.summary: A small review sample for a hospital this size — treat it as limited. One reviewer describes anesthesia and patient handling as dehumanizing at times, and says senior doctors don't always adequately supervise junior doctors, while still crediting doctors and staff generally as dedicated; they also note the hospital is enormous, with constantly long queues out front. In sharp contrast, another reviewer expresses deep gratitude to the cardiac ICU team for their care of her father around a transplant. A third reviewer makes a serious, unverified allegation that inadequate care and medication-swallowing difficulties contributed to their father's death from pneumonia during treatment. This is the Medical University of Warsaw's main clinical campus on Banacha street; Google Maps splits and renames some of its listings.

مستشفي ابو الريش الجامعي للاطفال بالمنير.summary: Widely praised as one of Egypt's best and largest children's hospitals, with reviewers describing dedicated staff working through resource shortages and overcrowded beds to treat kids from across the country, and several reviewers specifically urging the public to donate so more children can be treated for free. One reviewer's account is much harsher: alleging informal fees for bathroom access, parking, and even tea, plus a supervising trainee doctor dismissing an ear infection that an outside doctor later confirmed. Known in English as Abu El Reesh University Children's Hospital, affiliated with Cairo University.

bệnh viện chợ rẫy.summary: Ratings are polarized (1,627 five-star vs. 879 one-star out of 3,622). Specific complaints describe chaotic, overcrowded emergency room conditions with stretchers repeatedly colliding while patients wait, and multiple reviewers describe rude or bureaucratic treatment from staff — one paying patient objected to an orthopedic doctor's dismissive attitude, another said reasonable questions were met with rudeness. Review category tags include "neglect" and "fraud," suggesting more serious complaints exist beyond what's quoted here. Cho Ray Hospital is Vietnam's largest and most prestigious general hospital, drawing referred patients from across the southern part of the country, which likely contributes to the volume and overcrowding.

i̇stanbul üniversitesi tıp fakültesi has.summary: Reviewers commonly know this hospital by its old nickname, Çapa Hastanesi (Çapa Hospital), and one long-time local guide's review explains the lasting confusion between this hospital and the separately administered Cerrahpaşa Hospital, both historically part of Istanbul University's medical faculty before it split in two. A patient of 16 years in the general surgery department says they're very satisfied with the doctors and nurses, and another praises the whole team's performance and kindness. The rating distribution (57 five-star vs. 27 one-star out of 124) shows a real minority of negative experiences alongside the generally positive tone of the visible reviews.

karolinska universitetssjukhuset.summary: A family describes being moved immediately to a dedicated stroke ward after arriving with a father who'd had a stroke. Positive reviews describe kind doctors even for brief procedures, good food, and good rooms, and one patient thanks the whole team by name for a December surgery. A more mixed review praises skilled surgeons and compassionate night-shift staff but says understaffing caused real delays in pain medication and information, creating unnecessary stress. A sharply negative review alleges a missed medication dose that left the patient screaming in pain, a refusal to provide a sick note needed for their employer, young nurses on the ward discussing weekend plans instead of working, and never being allowed to speak with a doctor. One of Europe's leading research hospitals, affiliated with the Nobel Prize-awarding Karolinska Institute.

philippine general hospital.summary: One brief review credits the hospital with "giving my mom a second life." A recent surgery patient (a soft-palate lump removal) says they chose PGH first for its affordability and had heard good things from acquaintances treated there, and came away grateful. A longer review defends the hospital's aging-but-solid infrastructure and skilled doctors despite long waits and alleged government corruption, noting it's far cheaper than private hospitals and praising its artwork. On the negative side, a recent reviewer alleges being turned away and referred to a private hospital despite the ward appearing nearly empty, and describes the building as unsanitary and infection-prone; an older review (9 years ago) also called it slow and unsanitary. The country's largest public hospital, run by the University of the Philippines Manila, serving large numbers of lower-income patients.

clínica san ignacio.summary: The emergency department dominates recent complaints (147 mentions) and the reviews skew sharply negative. A new mother describes discriminatory treatment for her weight, being largely ignored by nursing staff after a C-section, and severe unmanaged pain — calling it traumatic enough that she doesn't want to have another child. Multiple other reviewers describe multi-hour to multi-day ER waits despite valid insurance referrals, one waiting 13 hours after being told by phone they'd be seen, another waiting 9 hours after arriving with a referral and being told to "come back tomorrow." One reviewer describes a specific doctor as dismissive and a nurse as distracted by social media during care. The hospital's official account replies to nearly every negative review with the same message directing complainants to its customer service email, suggesting a high, centrally managed complaint volume. Run by the Pontificia Universidad Javeriana, it's historically one of Colombia's top-ranked hospitals, and several reviewers note the decline is recent relative to its reputation.

newyork-presbyterian lower manhattan hos.summary: Maternity and the ER are the most-discussed topics. Multiple birth stories are very positive: a mother who delivered here 13 years ago and returned recently for minor surgery praises the staff both times, and another new mother thanks the entire delivery team — nurses, PA, OB, lactation consultant, and social worker — for a warm experience in a recently renovated facility. The ER draws similar praise: one reviewer calls it the best ER they've experienced, and a relative's injury was X-rayed, CT-scanned, and stitched within 3 hours. One dissenting note: a mother who delivered says the labor team was excellent but the separate postpartum recovery team was "a completely different experience."

new york eye and ear infirmary of mount.summary: Front-desk and phone-access issues dominate complaints — one reviewer waited over 24 hours for an antibiotic eye-drop prescription to reach their pharmacy despite multiple calls, with no MyChart or direct doctor access to escalate. On the positive side, ophthalmologist Dr. Paul Sidoti is praised by name for a thorough, reassuring annual exam after 30+ years of experience, with his assistant credited for the referral. A recent surgery patient was still awaiting their outcome and reserved judgment on the surgical team. The practice replies to negative reviews with a standard request to contact them directly, suggesting a high complaint volume relative to its specialty-clinic size.

lenox health greenwich village.summary: A Northwell Health free-standing ER with sharply mixed reviews. One reviewer names a specific physician, Dr. Steven Dernay, as dismissive and threatening to have her labeled a "problem patient" at Lenox Hill; a different reviewer alleges incompetent, profit-driven care that caused lasting harm and recommends going elsewhere entirely. In contrast, two nighttime ER visits over the past year were praised by name (Dr. Chris Davlantes and a nurse named Jose) for warmth and competence, and another visitor had a reasonably good experience despite a chaotic, crowded night. A separate serious complaint describes a security guard behaving in a hostile, intimidating way during a bag check at intake.

nyu langone orthopedic hospital.summary: A physician colleague of 20 years praises Dr. Lenart Sukhov's exceptional, dignified care, singling out his handling of her son's traumatic brain injury. A recent reviewer describes a complex reverse shoulder surgery that two other hospitals had declined as too difficult, successfully performed here with a named surgeon praised for kindness. On the negative side, one reviewer says quality has declined since the pandemic, describing a viral pneumonia sent home from the ER with only antibiotics that worsened into a bacterial infection; another cites repeated wrong-floor directions from the front desk causing a missed appointment; and a sciatica patient was seen quickly in the ortho ER but frustrated that no steroid injection was given for pain relief.

hoboken university medical center.summary: Maternity and the ER are the most-reviewed departments, with a wide quality gap between them. A father describes a very positive 3-day maternity stay with obstetrician Dr. Raki Patel, praising hourly nurse check-ins and a warm atmosphere. Same-day surgery is also praised: friendly nurses, an empathetic admin team, and a named surgeon (Dr. Ahn) in a modern (if dated-furniture) operating room. Ultrasound technologist Leena Patel is separately praised by name for thorough, attentive explanations. In sharp contrast, one reviewer describes a 6-hour ER wait for abdominal pain with no IV, only ibuprofen, a delayed ultrasound, and no doctor ever appearing before she left on her own.

jersey city medical center.summary: Consistently positive across departments, with reviewers repeatedly naming specific staff: physical therapists Dara and Brianna for gentle, attentive care of a 98-year-old patient; the radiology department for being organized and on-time; the women's ward and nursing staff for a laparoscopic endometriosis surgery; ultrasound technologist Christina for a patient, thorough scan; and oncology front-desk staff Shena and Melody for easing a frightened new cancer patient's first visit. The hospital's official account replies warmly to nearly every review. One of the more consistently well-reviewed large hospitals in the area.

hassenfeild children's hospital at nyu l.summary: Overwhelmingly positive. Multiple families describe the PICU staff — nurses, doctors, social workers, even cleaning staff — as treating their children like family; one family's 3-year-old had heart surgery under Dr. Mosca, with staff praised for keeping them informed throughout and answering every question. Reviewers also highlight the building itself: child-friendly art meant to ease hospital fear, a modern design with striking views, and large TVs in patient rooms. No significant complaints appear in the visible reviews.

brooklyn hospital center.summary: A very small review sample for a hospital this size — treat it as limited. One recent, detailed complaint describes a 12-hour ER visit for her daughter with no diagnosis, no doctor follow-up, dismissive staff, and no IV pole available; she ultimately left to drive to another hospital instead. Another reviewer describes a 4-hour wait resulting only in antibiotics with no other treatment. On the positive side, ER staff are thanked for patience with a non-English-speaking family during an overnight stay, and nuclear medicine specialist Dr. Christine Perez is praised by name for her respectful, kind treatment of an elderly patient.

nyu langone outpatient surgery center.summary: A small but mostly positive sample. One patient praises Dr. Traube and says every staff member, down to the cleaning crew, made the visit feel warm and unhurried. A radiologic technologist, Dennis Nichols, is separately praised for patiently mentoring an intern while still attentively answering the reviewer's own questions. On the negative side, one reviewer witnessed a security guard harass a woman sleeping in the waiting room without cause, another had a frustrating billing interaction over a cash payment, and a trigger-finger surgery patient (a 3-minute local-anesthesia procedure) was annoyed at being told to arrive 90 minutes early with no specific reason given.

veteran affairs new york harbor healthca.summary: Reviews are notably split between strong praise for specific staff and broader skepticism about VA care quality. A neurosurgery patient praises Dr. Miller by name (parking is the only real complaint); another describes excellent surgical care plus a considerate overnight phone staff during a busy shift. A kidney-stone surgery patient chose this VA over Mount Sinai or NewYork-Presbyterian for continuity of 6 years of records, calling the surgery itself excellent despite a difficult recovery at home afterward. On the more critical side, one long-time patient advises getting referred out to non-VA care as soon as possible, calling VA staff quality "below average" on the whole; another notes the benefit of NYU teaching staff providing modern overnight coverage, offset by the discomfort of being treated by supervised residents and interns still training.

los angeles general medical center.summary: A high-volume county safety-net hospital with reviews reflecting both its scale and its strain. One family describes excellent doctor care across two serious admissions (third-degree burns and a burst vein), with only nursing attitude as a complaint. Others describe real access problems: one patient saw five different doctors with inconsistent diagnoses and a referral wait of 3+ weeks; another calls it "one of the worst hospitals in the world" after a 90-minute ER wait with severe kidney stones; a nurse reportedly forgot a child's second antibiotic dose during a 24-hour ER stay. Balancing this, one family thanks the staff by name for a month and a half of care that they say saved their brother's life. Formerly known as LAC+USC Medical Center, it's affiliated with USC's medical school.

white memorial medical center.summary: Consistently warm reviews with many named staff: a nursing team praised for calling a patient's mother "mom" with genuine compassion; a pacemaker procedure credited to Dr. Salazar and an attentive on-call team; a surgery patient thanks Dr. Salem's surgical team and a long list of named ICU and monitoring-unit staff; two nurses (Crystal and Jessica) singled out on the 3rd floor; and an outpatient procedure patient recounts good-natured, attentive service down to a lost phone returned by security. Now operating as Adventist Health White Memorial.

good samaritan hospital.summary: Reviews (several written in Korean, reflecting the hospital's proximity to Koreatown) are sharply mixed. Positive accounts describe a kind, attentive staff from admission on, clean daily-serviced rooms, and a pre/post-surgical recovery floor (4th floor) praised as quiet, professional, and comfortable. On the negative side, one reviewer names a specific 5th-floor nurse as unresponsive and unqualified and wants to file a formal complaint, and another says the hospital has become noticeably less attentive and more indifferent than in the past. Operates as PIH Health Good Samaritan Hospital.

usc norris cancer hospital.summary: A specialized cancer hospital with uniformly positive reviews. One patient describes being transferred here from another USC facility after an AML (acute myeloid leukemia) diagnosis; another credits the entire admission-to-discharge team, including a named surgeon and PA team, with treating them as a person, not just a patient. A radiation therapy patient, now in remission, thanks Dr. Yeh and staff member Daniel by name; a radiation oncology patient separately praises Dr. Lim for patient, thorough explanations throughout treatment. Part of Keck Medicine of USC, next door to Keck Hospital of USC.

california hospital medical center.summary: Reviews (several written in Korean) are generally positive but note slow service at times: one endoscopy patient praised the cleanliness and attentiveness but waited from 6am to 10am for a routine procedure; another says biopsy results took over a week to reach them despite the staff otherwise being kind. On the positive side, a patient who'd seen multiple other providers without a diagnosis says this hospital finally identified their knee problem and helped them get needed insurance approval, and another calls a recent ER visit fast and better than expected. Operates as Dignity Health - California Hospital Medical Center.

gateways hospital.summary: A psychiatric hospital, so reviews reflect inpatient mental health treatment rather than general medicine. A former teenage patient (admitted in 2012 after a suicide attempt) says the care helped set him on a path to now working as a clinical social worker himself, and another patient's multi-week stay is recalled with generally warm memories of specific staff by nickname. A mother recounts her son's psychiatric hospitalization after she flew in from South Africa, wishing a specific psychiatrist had shown more warmth given how frightening and disorienting the situation was for the family. A separate, unrelated complaint describes ongoing construction noise disrupting the surrounding neighborhood.

keck hospital of usc.summary: A large academic medical center with mixed reviews. A family thanks the surgical team for a mother's major surgery and recovery, calling the team's skill and warmth transformative during a hard time. On the more serious side, one reviewer alleges a mammogram was misread and missed a tumor, prompting a second opinion elsewhere and a since-confirmed cancer diagnosis — a serious, unverified claim. Another describes a distressing post-surgical phone call about active bleeding where the call center repeatedly asked to re-verify a phone number instead of addressing the emergency. A separate complaint concerns poorly maintained EV chargers in the parking structure. Part of Keck Medicine of USC.

barlow respiratory hospital.summary: A specialized long-term acute care hospital for ventilator weaning and respiratory rehab, so reviews differ from a general hospital's. One reviewer, having compared four LA hospitals, calls this the worst, alleging no patient was discharged in 4 months during their family's experience. Others are warmly positive: a nurse (Analisa Muiruri) is thanked by name for compassionate care of a father-in-law, and another family found the nursing staff empathetic during a difficult time. One pointed, angry review accuses the hospital of billing Medicare/Medi-Cal heavily per day after a patient's death, while still listing several attending physicians and staff by name.

kaiser foundation hospital mental health.summary: A Kaiser Permanente inpatient psychiatric facility; reviews describe a wide range of experiences. Positive accounts describe kind nursing staff, a psychiatrist who listened carefully, and a partial hospitalization (PHP) program credited with resolving a serious crisis. A more troubling account describes a patient discharged after 4 days who relapsed and was readmitted within another 4 days. One serious, unverified allegation describes a patient held under an involuntary psychiatric hold being told to consent to electroconvulsive therapy (ECT) or face a 180-day extended hold, describing the resulting consent as coerced and alleging lasting harm. As with other Kaiser facilities, care here is generally restricted to Kaiser Permanente health plan members.

joshua house health center.summary: A free community health clinic in Skid Row (run by LA Christian Health Centers), not a full hospital. Reviewers consistently praise the doctors as patient and caring — one specifically rates them more professional than other local low-cost providers — and a same-day knee X-ray appointment drew particular gratitude. A more critical review says front-desk service has declined over the years, citing unwritten, arbitrarily enforced policies and wait times comparable to a private practice, with walk-in visits especially difficult.

ann & robert h. lurie children's hospita.summary: A well-regarded children's hospital, though ER wait times are a recurring theme. One parent describes a longer-than-expected visit eased by attentive, kind staff who brought snacks and water for hungry kids; another's child was admitted for 3 days — the ER wait was long but expected, and inpatient care was excellent throughout. An adult patient (seen by a specialist who also treats children) loves the hospital's art, sculptures, and cafeteria, naming her immunologist Dr. Kim as outstanding. Another parent describes a brain scan that correctly diagnosed a child's seizures, followed by medication that helped significantly.

rush university medical center.summary: Ratings are sharply bimodal (574 five-star vs. 404 one-star out of 1,187), and recent reviews skew toward frustration. One mother filed a formal complaint after a delayed appointment for her daughter; another describes a bleeding injury in the ER where a doctor refused to say whether stitches were needed and deprioritized the case for something "more important"; a reviewer who came for a second opinion says the physician was satisfactory but the entire experience was overshadowed by a confusing, frustrating billing process. The hospital's official account replies to each with the same request to contact patient relations directly.

university of illinois at chicago hospit.summary: A patient who traveled 3 hours for a "life-changing" surgery praises attentive staff who brought warm blankets, explained every step, and helped arrange lodging. Another thanks the medical team for excellent care of their father, while flagging two unspecified process issues that kept it from a perfect rating. A pregnant patient describes serious, repeated insurance-verification problems despite having both union coverage and Medicaid, causing delayed prenatal care and added stress. A harsher review alleges rude, unprofessional staff and a urinal left beside food trays for hours. Separately, a patient alleges her pain was dismissed during a breast cyst procedure — a serious, unverified allegation of being disbelieved. Operates as UI Health.

jesse brown va medical center.summary: One veteran thanks the staff for consistent respect, naming VA police officer Joseph Dais specifically, and says the "90% good, honest people" shouldn't be defined by a "bad 10%." A more critical reviewer calls it the "ghetto VA," saying it lives up to that reputation, without much detail. A detailed complaint describes a disabled veteran's ER visit with his son: a promised EKG was never done, an anti-nausea medication was never brought despite a nurse saying she'd get it, only a PICC line was placed with no fluids given, and most of the blood/urine samples taken were never actually sent out of the room.

john h. stroger, jr. hospital of cook co.summary: A couple describes their first-pregnancy checkups as professional, warm, and attentive from arrival. A disabled patient credits four named staff members (Carolina Vasquez, Regina Bethel, Alex Argueta, and Linda James) with excellent teamwork — fast prescriptions and refills, and even catching medication errors made at other hospitals. On the negative side, one reviewer describes staff frequently on their phones, passing off responsibilities, and poor communication between departments. Cook County's public safety-net hospital, part of Cook County Health.

insight hospital & medical center.summary: One reviewer praises a clean, well-maintained Islamic prayer room with ample parking. Nurse Megan (dual RN/CNA-certified) is singled out for excellent care despite understaffing, and an imaging/records staff member named Ciara is thanked for prompt, professional help with delayed paperwork. On the negative side, one reviewer describes a cascade of billing errors — incorrect charges, double-billing, fees for cancelled appointments, a non-functional online payment system, and no resolution after multiple calls. A separate reviewer says a prior review describing a disturbing interaction with Dr. Marco Rodriguez over a father's discharge was removed from Google.

saint joseph medical center.summary: A patient dreading a follow-up visit after a bad prior experience says this one completely changed her mind — professional, nonjudgmental staff throughout, with a phlebotomist singled out as the best she's ever had. Another reviewer, whose husband dislikes hospitals after past bad experiences, says the front desk, security, nurses, and doctors were all so kind that he too came away satisfied. A third thanks the ICU team for attentive, comforting care of her mother during a stroke and pneumonia admission.

park plaza hospital.summary: Mostly strongly positive: one patient praises the ER and 9th-floor-south nursing staff, the on-call doctors, a Dr. Yu, and even radiology, housekeeping, and dietary staff by department. A nurse named Marsha is singled out for calmly running an entire post-op ward solo overnight without ever making the patient feel rushed. Another thanks a newly-hired ER patient coordinator, a prenatal nurse, a Dr. Ryan K, and the CT tech by name. On the negative side, one reviewer says intermediate-care nursing was good, but she wasn't given her daily medications or anything for pain/nausea on the first night and had to take pills she'd brought from home herself, with IV fluids taking hours to get ordered. Operates as HCA Houston Healthcare Medical Center.

plaza specialty hospital.summary: A small review sample for a long-term acute care hospital — treat it as limited. Reviewers consistently name specific staff: a case worker (Regina Clark) and nurse (Tiffany) praised for preparing a family to bring their mother home; a staff member nicknamed "George B." praised for warmth and even magic tricks that lighten the mood; nurses Norma and Courtney Fellerin thanked by name. One more mixed review describes a father transferred here from Ben Taub Hospital to wean off a ventilator — most nurses were excellent, though a few caused anxious nights, and a visiting-hours conflict briefly kept the family from seeing him. Operates as AMG Specialty Hospital - Houston Medical Center.

children's hospital of philadelphia.summary: A reviewer calls the care and kindness from doctors, nurses, and everyone else at CHOP amazing. A frustrated reviewer alleges inconsistent, confusing daily rules around bringing a personal mobility scooter through security, being stopped repeatedly despite prior permission. On the very positive side, a family describes world-class care for their child from the ER through specialists, crediting Child Life Specialists with keeping their child calm and safe during tests and procedures, and praising the state-of-the-art facility and dedicated staff.

thomas jefferson university hospital.summary: A patient who arrived with sudden vision loss via the Wills Eye ER connection says Jefferson's staff kept her calm and reassured throughout, especially a front-desk nurse she couldn't name. A glowing birth story credits Dr. Madeline Rosado and names several postpartum nurses (Gina, Kelly, Alissa) for excellent care, plus a second anesthesiologist who took her pain seriously and delivered a painless epidural. Another couple praises the entire team — admission through discharge — for an emergency involving her husband.

wills eye hospital.summary: A recurring complaint is cost and wait times rather than clinical care: one reviewer calls the ER good but the main hospital "the worst," citing a 90-minute wait past a scheduled appointment and $30 parking; another's mother loves her ophthalmologist but faced a long wait to actually see the doctor and was charged $36 for 2 hours of parking despite a quoted discount. A more serious complaint describes a scary miscommunication when front-desk staff failed to leave a message after an after-hours call about a parent's surgery recovery. On the positive side, Dr. Whitney Jamison is praised by name for gentle, on-time, pain-free care, and a long-time patient says Dr. Michael Cohen is the only eye doctor he trusts, having followed him to this hospital specifically.

penn presbyterian medical center.summary: A daughter whose mother had repeated ER visits (dislocated shoulders, low sodium, leg swelling) says the familiarity and monitoring she'd come to know from past visits was reassuring. A hip-surgery patient's family praises the 5S ward's nurses, especially one named Paul, called a "superhero." On the negative side, one reviewer says no transport staff were available to move her 85-year-old mother from the elevator to outpatient surgery, forcing her to push a wheelchair and pull a walker herself, plus a 30-minute wait over lost paperwork despite an empty line. Another says eye-surgery OR staff were excellent but docked stars for a dirty waiting-room floor and bathroom.

pennsylvania hospital.summary: Consistently positive, with many named staff: pre-op nurse True and Drs. Spears and Frankl praised for a reassuring outpatient surgery, with OR nurse Ryan called knowledgeable and warm; a radiology patient praises the whole department for a thorough, calming visit; Dr. Batul is credited with a smooth, well-explained appendectomy; a reviewer says Penn's ER caught a bowel obstruction that, in their account, Temple Hospital had missed the day before, leading to same-day emergency surgery and, two months later, a tumor-removal surgery, with 6th-floor staff across nursing, medicine, and therapy all praised for support through a frightening experience.

corporal michael j. crescenz veterans af.summary: A harsh complaint describes the Community Care coordination team as inattentive — mispronouncing patient names, calling at inconvenient times, no voicemails on missed calls, and over an hour on hold. In contrast, a veteran of 45 years with this VA says staff have always been respectful and kind across many departments (endocrinology, neurology, ENT, mental health, podiatry, nephrology, MRI, ophthalmology) with only minor, quickly-resolved issues. Another visitor compares the facility's cleanliness unfavorably to prisons she'd worked in, during her husband's MRI visit. A mental-health-focused patient says therapy and counseling have been excellent but physical-health care is inconsistent, with some nurses contradicting doctors and reacting poorly to being quoted their own supervisor's guidance.

cooper university hospital.summary: A serious complaint describes a 5-hour wait in Camden for a medication the reviewer says is normally administered in 30 minutes and needed urgently. On the positive side, a birth story credits Dr. Schaefer, Dr. Carolyn Ross, and Dr. Amanda Malik with attentive prenatal-through-delivery care, with postpartum nurse Sheila named specifically; a 90-year-old patient's MD Anderson-referred cancer care in the ER and oncology ward is praised as exceeding expectations. A separate complaint alleges Cooper sent decade-old medical debt to collections without ever sending a bill, statement, or insurance-denial notice in 7 years, raising statute-of-limitations concerns.

temple university hospital - episcopal c.summary: Ratings are notably low, with several serious allegations: one reviewer says she was left to vomit on herself in bed and discharged in inadequate clothing in freezing weather; another alleges waking up from a seizure without shoes or clothes to nurses who were dismissive and allegedly laughed while she cried, then denied her a visitor and gave no IV or workup when she objected; a third describes ER security staff behaving so badly toward his wife that he calls for the location to be shut down, after being unable to reach anyone by phone across four numbers. These are serious, unverified allegations. On the positive side, one reviewer's father had a comparatively quick (3-hour) and friendly ER visit, and the mammography department is specifically praised as excellent and caring.

girard medical center.summary: A behavioral-health and addiction-treatment facility (operating as The Behavioral Wellness Center at Girard), with mixed reviews. One reviewer describes rude, unprofessional front-desk staff arguing in view of patients while picking up a sibling's medication. A more serious allegation claims substance-abuse counselors encouraged patients toward relapse-risk behavior (taking others' prescriptions) and that a staff member dismissed the reviewer's ethics concerns. Another describes broken air conditioning during severe weather, constant room intrusions, and feeling unsafe amid other residents despite having disabilities that put her at fall risk on stairs. On the positive side, one reviewer credits staff with helping cover medical costs during admission and says he's maintained 9 years of sobriety since; another praises the nurses and therapists as the most helpful of any facility they've used.

kensington hospital.summary: A small community hospital with mixed-to-positive reviews. A patient hoping for a reliable local primary-care doctor was disappointed after an initially promising first visit. An outpatient pulmonology patient thanks the department's doctor and staff and calls the hospital clean. A patient who spent over a month in inpatient addiction treatment, despite initial fear and uncertainty, says every staff member was kind, empathetic, and professional. Another, who first came at 17 for addiction treatment and returned twice more over the years (as did some family members), describes it as a place that genuinely helps those who want it.

kirkbride center.summary: A drug and alcohol treatment and detox center with a consistently difficult reputation in reviews. One reviewer credits three named staff (Dr. Wyckoff, Tina, and Bonnie) as the sole reason for even 3 stars, describing the facility itself as barely more than a shelter and security staff as rude to visiting family. A patient with multiple stays, including an 8-month stint, describes most staff as disengaged and frequently on their phones. Several separate reviews name a specific front-desk staff member as unprofessional and unkind toward patients seeking treatment.
