Phone-based intake staff are also described as cold and unsympathetic in arranging basic family contact.

jefferson methodist hospital.summary: Consistently positive. A longtime patient credits the Jefferson Headache Center and its doctors and nurses for never rushing her and always treating her like their only patient. A first-time visitor praises easy parking and friendly security-to-registration staff, with Dr. Jung's thorough 20-minute pre-surgical consultation singled out. A 4th-floor nurse named Daniel and podiatrist Dr. Green are both praised by name, and a same-day ER-to-discharge (12 hours) experience is described as attentive and professional throughout.

jefferson moss-magee rehabilitation hosp.summary: A well-known inpatient rehabilitation hospital (Magee Rehab) with overwhelmingly positive reviews. Patients repeatedly name specific physicians (Dr. Messer, Dr. Levin, Dr. Kuzer) and large teams of therapists by first name for patient, encouraging, highly individualized care through recovery from strokes, spinal cord injuries, and trauma. One reviewer, still mid-recovery, says every therapist and doctor made her feel genuinely cared for even without a full recovery yet. Multiple reviewers describe the hospital as having become like family during a long rehabilitation process.

penn medicine rittenhouse.summary: A long-term acute care and rehabilitation site, often used for patients transferred from an ICU. One reviewer thanks nurses, orderlies, dietary staff, and the physical therapy team by department for helping him recover safely. A sharply negative review warns against the facility's rehab program entirely, without detail. Another flags a billing concern: doctors reportedly ordered tests not covered by insurance without informing the patient beforehand that they'd be billed directly. A particularly difficult account describes a husband transferred here from the ICU for pneumonia and lung-cancer complications requiring high-flow oxygen — nursing care was good, but the family found it distressing that social workers and counselors raised the question of starting home hospice three times within a few days.

boston children's hospital.summary: A very small review sample for a hospital of this size — treat it as limited, since most of the hospital's patient feedback is split across department-level listings. Visible reviews are all positive ("the best hospital I've ever been to", kind staff, a donor praising the blood-donation team), and the hospital's own listing highlights its #1 pediatrics ranking on Newsweek's 2027 World's Best Specialized Hospitals list.

brigham and women's hospital.summary: Sharply bimodal (356 five-star vs. 258 one-star out of 709). A spine-surgery patient reports outstanding results and credits the nurses entirely for making his recovery possible, urging the system to pay them properly. Complaints include unhelpful, hard-to-reach customer support, a patient unable to find a primary-care doctor for over a year, an alleged dispute with security guards at the Francis Street lobby over parking, and a distressing account from a family with a relative dying in the ICU who say a nurse lied and then retaliated against them — a serious, unverified allegation.

beth israel deaconess medical center eas.summary: Overwhelmingly positive in the visible reviews (2,345 five-star vs. 301 one-star out of 2,836), though much of this listing's feedback concerns its orthopedic and spine practices — Drs. Ramappa, Davis, and Friedberg are each praised by name for careful listening and excellent surgical results (shoulder, bicep tendon, rotator cuff). Review snippets also praise the ICU team and staff kindness; one patient complained a kitchen refused a meal order after a day of fasting. Google combines the East and West Campus buildings under this one listing.

beth israel deaconess medical center wes.summary: Overwhelmingly positive in the visible reviews (2,345 five-star vs. 301 one-star out of 2,836), though much of this listing's feedback concerns its orthopedic and spine practices — Drs. Ramappa, Davis, and Friedberg are each praised by name for careful listening and excellent surgical results (shoulder, bicep tendon, rotator cuff). Review snippets also praise the ICU team and staff kindness; one patient complained a kitchen refused a meal order after a day of fasting. Google combines the East and West Campus buildings under this one listing.

dana-farber cancer institute.summary: A cancer treatment center where the visible feedback is limited: highlighted reviews call it a "great place for cancer treatments" with wonderful doctors, and one patient who describes themselves as picky says the care was excellent. Reviews of its individual treatment-center sub-listings (breast, head and neck, sarcoma, Jimmy Fund Clinic for children at 4.5★) are similarly positive but each have very few ratings; the hematologic oncology sub-listing has a single 1-star rating with no detail.

tufts medical center.summary: Split between devoted praise and frustration (290 five-star vs. 240 one-star out of 618). Visible reviews are strongly positive about specific units: a family whose sister spent two years on the North 8 oncology floor says the nurses and doctors "genuinely loved" her, a father credits Dr. Klein's team on the same floor through his daughter's 9-month cancer battle, the 4 North surgical floor staff are called amazing and compassionate, and two reviewers praise labor-and-delivery staff, one saying the contrast with another hospital's care was dramatic.

boston medical center.summary: Boston's largest safety-net hospital, with sharply bimodal ratings (383 five-star vs. 335 one-star out of 855) and the ER the most-discussed topic. Visible reviews are warm: a labor nurse named Carrie Smith is praised for caring for both a patient and her spouse, the Menino Pavilion team (nurses, social worker, case manager) is thanked for compassion toward an elderly patient, Dr. Morgan Harloff is credited with a successful valve replacement and clear explanations, and a five-year patient reports no bad experiences including pharmacy service.

massachusetts eye and ear.summary: Reviews highlight the emergency department and long waits: Google's own summary describes "great people but understaffed and not enough rooms." One ED patient says staff were kind and handled his issue rapidly; another complains of being swiftly dismissed on a follow-up question to a surgeon's office and calls the front-line handling unprofessional; a diner singles out the cafeteria chef for an excellent lunch. Individual surgeons at this campus hold near-perfect ratings on their own listings.

va medical center - seattle.summary: Mostly positive in visible reviews. One veteran who's used several VA medical centers calls Seattle "by far the best," praising its clean, well-kept facility and parking garage and friendly staff who walked him to his destination. Two separate total-knee-replacement patients credit orthopedic surgeon Dr. Chansky and the nursing, physical-therapy, and occupational-therapy staff at every stage; a patient seen here since 2021 reports consistently high-quality care despite the facility being "a bit of a maze." The sharpest complaint says it was once great but now it's impossible to schedule appointments, with phone staff passing callers around without taking accountability.

kaiser permanente capitol hill campus.summary: Review topics skew strongly positive — "friendly staff" (206 mentions), "caring staff" (92), "thoroughness" (46), and "clear explanations" (25) — with wait time (92 mentions) the main recurring friction point. The campus's separate Urgent Care listing at the same address is rated much lower (2.5★ from 129 reviews), so experiences differ sharply between the main clinic and urgent care. I wasn't able to read individual review text for this listing, so this summary is based on Google's own topic counts and ratings only.

swedish first hill medical center.summary: Strongly positive, with "caring staff" the top topic by far (87 mentions). Reviewers describe exceptional nursing and support staff, one saying it was his seventh surgery and by far the best experience in terms of cleanliness, communication, and timeliness; another praises the Swedish Neuroscience Institute, where Dr. Monteith and his team quickly saw and treated a complex cerebral aneurysm. Wait time (20 mentions) is the most common complaint. Google lists this as "Swedish Hospital - First Hill Campus."

swedish medical center cherry hill campu.summary: Mixed. Surgical and cardiac care draws praise: a husband's brain surgery under Dr. Miri Kim is credited with professional, caring staff from admission through the ICU, and an outpatient echocardiogram patient praised a nursing assistant who had just become an RN. Administrative and billing issues draw complaints: one patient of nearly 20 years was surprised by a $410 bill for a routine 40-minute telehealth visit with a resident, another describes a rude phone scheduler and a 10-day wait for an appointment callback, and a third had a distressing testing experience in which she felt she wasn't taken seriously.

baylor university medical center.summary: Warmly reviewed overall: "caring staff" is the top topic (205 mentions). Visible reviews praise labor-and-delivery nurses from triage onward, an obstetrician credited by name after six years of care through delivery, a kidney-transplant patient celebrating a two-year transplant anniversary with the Simmons Transplant Institute team, and a first-time patient impressed by how quickly check-in went. Wait time (75 mentions) is the most common friction point. Part of Baylor Scott & White Health.

methodist dallas medical center.summary: Overwhelmingly positive in visible reviews, with "friendly staff" (404 mentions) and "caring staff" (150) leading. A husband describes emergency surgery for his wife and names four nurses and the ER team as thorough and caring; a patient thanks Dr. David Levine and his team for kindness and respect; a family credits the 4th-floor ICU day and night shifts after a liver transplant at the Methodist Liver Institute; another reviewer praises the nurses, doctors, and lactation consultants after a birth. Wait times (54 mentions) are the main recurring complaint.

texas scottish rite hospital for childre.summary: A specialty children's orthopedic hospital with uniformly glowing reviews. One family has brought their son here for 9 years; another describes a daughter's recent spinal fusion — they've been patients since she was 12 — praising nurses, doctors, security, volunteers, and facility alike; a parent describes staff making their son feel comfortable at a casting visit; and a patient names Dr. Hubbard as especially good at listening. Wait time (10 mentions) is the only recurring minor complaint. Google lists it as "Dallas Scottish Rite for Children."

baylor scott & white heart and vascular.summary: A specialty cardiac hospital with very high ratings. A mother who traveled from Houston for her daughter's specialized surgery found the hospital clean and the staff caring; a sleep-study patient describes an extraordinary experience and thanks three staff by name; another reviewer who brought an aunt for a heart check says everyone, especially the nurses, was helpful though the building is "like a maze." Google's own highlighted snippets include two criticisms: a patient whose keys were thrown away by cleaning staff, and a complaint about poor communication between staff.

phoenix children's hospital.summary: Mixed. Parents praise individual staff — a nurse named Amber for compassionate care during their daughter's surgery, and a dermatology clinic team for warmth — but waits are the recurring theme (emergency department 143 mentions, wait time 115) and "rude staff" appears 26 times. One parent complained in 2026 that staff still restricted both parents from entering for COVID reasons; another said a second transport stay for their baby was the "complete opposite" of a compassionate first; and grandparents of a disabled, diabetic child described a defensive reaction from the endocrinology floor lead when they called for information. The ER sub-listing is rated lower (2.5★ from 221 reviews). Google lists the main campus as "Thomas Campus."

valleywise health medical center.summary: Maricopa County's safety-net hospital, with mixed reviews. One recent ER patient called everyone from registration to nursing wonderful; another describes a "nice new hospital" serving the surrounding community and jail inmates, run by an understaffed, overworked team. Google's highlighted snippets include a reviewer who says staff and nurses "have become family," and others warning visitors to bring their own food and medications and not to count on dental abscess care. An out-of-town visitor describes a diagnosis that took until day 5 of a 7-day trip after he presented with breathing difficulty and shoulder-blade pain — an account of a delayed diagnosis from a single reviewer. The ER sub-listing is rated 2.7★ from 102 reviews.

dignity health st joseph's hospital and.summary: I could read only the listing-level ratings for this hospital, not individual reviews: the main listing is rated 4.1★ from 2,732 reviews, and its emergency room has a separate listing at 4.2★ from 1,598 reviews. Two other listings at the same address are much lower (2.8★ from 81 reviews, and 1.9★ from 33), so it's worth reading recent reviews directly before relying on the main rating.

uc san diego medical center.summary: Mixed. Visible reviews praise the ER (a patient who feared a heart attack was treated well for dehydration), a fast CT scan with results in two hours, and the care of one family whose husband was injured in a fall and treated at Hillcrest. One reviewer who was a patient at the system's La Jolla hospital says Hillcrest was by far the better experience. A serious, unverified allegation from a husband claims his wife was mistreated and mocked while recovering from anesthesia. "Nurses" is the top review topic (87 mentions). Google lists this campus as "Hillcrest Medical Center at UC San Diego Health."

scripps mercy hospital.summary: Mixed, with strong praise for maternity and surgical-floor nursing. A mother of three says the nurses were kind and supportive throughout her third delivery; a reviewer's sister spent weeks on the 5th floor after multiple leg surgeries and called every nurse phenomenal; another couple found the facilities and nurses high-end and thorough. On the negative side, a nurse practitioner with 13 years' experience said she was deeply disappointed with her same-day surgery experience, one patient complained of a rough IV removal and rude doctors, and wait time (33 mentions) is a recurring theme.
